root_cause.text: The nft_set_pipapo commit-time GC freed expired elements too early—during scanning of the clone before the live `match` pointer was swapped—so readers on the packet path or userspace dumpers could still access those elements from the old live structure, causing a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states “We cannot queue elements for freeing until pointers have been swapped” and that “call_rcu() does not protect us” because lookups/dumps can still observe freed elements; correspondingly, the patch changes `pipapo_gc()` into `pipapo_gc_scan()` that only unlinks/collects elements into `priv->gc_head`, then defers actual freeing with `pipapo_gc_queue(set)` until after `rcu_replace_pointer(priv->match, priv->clone, ...)` in `nft_pipapo_commit()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an inline helper to compute remaining nft_trans_gc batch space for reusable capacity checks.
intent_record.what: A new static inline helper function named nft_trans_gc_space(const struct nft_trans_gc *trans) was added, which returns NFT_TRANS_GC_BATCHCOUNT - trans->count.
intent_record.how: This introduces a reusable way to compute the remaining capacity in an nft_trans_gc batch at runtime, enabling callers to query how many entries are still available instead of recalculating the expression manually.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the redundant nft_trans_gc_space() helper that only wrapped a simple batch-space calculation.
intent_record.what: A static helper function named nft_trans_gc_space() was removed; the deleted function returned NFT_TRANS_GC_BATCHCOUNT - trans->count and no replacement is shown in this hunk.
intent_record.how: This eliminates a wrapper that computed remaining GC batch space, likely because the function was unused or its logic is being inlined elsewhere; by itself, this hunk does not introduce a direct runtime behavior change.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rename the pipapo GC helper to `pipapo_gc_scan` and update its comment to reflect that it scans expired entries and queues them on a GC list.
intent_record.what: The function comment was updated to rename `pipapo_gc()` to `pipapo_gc_scan()` and to change its description from dropping expired entries and destroying start/end elements to dropping expired entries and linking them to a GC list; the static function definition was also renamed from `pipapo_gc` to `pipapo_gc_scan` with no other code changes shown.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the visible effect is only that the function is now identified by a new name that better matches a scan-oriented garbage-collection role; based on the updated comment, the intended behavior is to collect expired entries into a garbage-collection list rather than destroy elements directly, but this hunk itself only shows the rename and documentation update.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the newly allocated GC entry in `priv->gc_head` so pipapo garbage-collection state is properly tracked and cleaned up.
intent_record.what: A new statement was added in `pipapo_gc()` after the null check for `gc`: `list_add(&gc->list, &priv->gc_head);`, which inserts the `gc->list` node into the `priv->gc_head` linked list before entering the existing `while` loop.
intent_record.how: At runtime, any non-null garbage-collection object created or obtained in `pipapo_gc()` is now registered on `priv->gc_head` immediately, ensuring it is tracked by the set's GC list during subsequent processing instead of remaining unlinked and potentially omitted from later cleanup or lifecycle management.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix pipapo garbage collection to allocate and queue a new GC transaction only when the current one has no space, instead of synchronizing on every expired element.
intent_record.what: The code in pipapo_gc() replaces an unconditional call to nft_trans_gc_queue_sync(gc, GFP_KERNEL) with a conditional capacity check using nft_trans_gc_space(gc); when no space is available, it allocates a new GC transaction via nft_trans_gc_alloc(set, 0, GFP_KERNEL), returns on allocation failure, and adds the new transaction to priv->gc_head with list_add(&gc->list, &priv->gc_head).
intent_record.how: At runtime, expired elements are now added to an existing GC transaction as long as it has room, and a new GC transaction is allocated and linked only when needed. This avoids forcing synchronous queue handling on every expired element and ensures garbage-collection work is accumulated in available transaction objects before creating another one.

intent_record.intent_summary: Split pipapo GC queuing into a dedicated helper so catchall and deferred GC entries are always flushed correctly after expiration processing.
intent_record.what: The code removes the tail of `pipapo_gc()` that called `nft_trans_gc_catchall_sync(gc)`, conditionally queued the resulting GC transaction with `nft_trans_gc_queue_sync_done(gc)`, and updated `priv->last_gc = jiffies;`, leaving `pipapo_gc()` to only set `priv->last_gc = jiffies;`. It then adds a new function `pipapo_gc_queue(struct nft_set *set)` that obtains `priv`, allocates a catchall GC transaction with `nft_trans_gc_alloc(set, 0, GFP_KERNEL)`, runs it through `nft_trans_gc_catchall_sync(gc)`, queues it with `nft_trans_gc_queue_sync_done(gc)` if still valid, and finally iterates over `priv->gc_head` with `list_for_each_entry_safe()` to delete each queued entry from the list and submit it via `nft_trans_gc_queue_sync_done(gc)`.
intent_record.how: Runtime behavior is changed by separating garbage-collection scanning from garbage-collection queuing. `pipapo_gc()` now only performs expiry processing and records the GC timestamp, while the new `pipapo_gc_queue()` explicitly performs a catchall GC cycle and flushes any previously queued GC entries from `priv->gc_head`. This ensures deferred GC elements are always purged and synchronization-completion work is always queued through a dedicated path instead of being tied only to the end of `pipapo_gc()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Document that nft_pipapo_commit() can queue expired elements for reclamation after swapping the live copy with the clone.
intent_record.what: The change adds four comment lines to the documentation block above nft_pipapo_commit(), explaining that after replacing the live copy with the clone, expired elements collected by pipapo_gc_scan() can be safely queued for memory reclaim.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior; it clarifies the point in the commit flow at which reclaiming expired elements is considered safe.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the scan-based pipapo garbage-collection routine during commit so expired entries are cleaned with the correct logic before publishing the cloned match structure.
intent_record.what: The call inside nft_pipapo_commit() was changed from pipapo_gc(set, priv->clone) to pipapo_gc_scan(set, priv->clone) when the garbage-collection interval condition is met.
intent_record.how: At commit time, the code now invokes a different garbage-collection routine on the clone set, which changes the runtime cleanup behavior performed before replacing the active match structure and likely ensures the correct scan-based GC logic is used in this path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Queue pipapo garbage collection after commit so post-commit cleanup work is reliably scheduled.
intent_record.what: A new call to pipapo_gc_queue(set); was added at the end of nft_pipapo_commit(), after the existing conditional call_rcu(&old->rcu, pipapo_reclaim_match); block.
intent_record.how: After committing changes to the pipapo set, the function now explicitly queues garbage collection work for the set, ensuring deferred cleanup or expiration processing is scheduled following a successful commit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize priv->gc_head during nft_pipapo setup to avoid later garbage-collection operations using an uninitialized list head.
intent_record.what: A new initialization call, INIT_LIST_HEAD(&priv->gc_head), was added in nft_pipapo_init() just before assigning priv->match with rcu_assign_pointer().
intent_record.how: This ensures the gc_head list in the private set state is initialized to an empty valid list before any later garbage-collection list operations occur, preventing use of an uninitialized list head at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a one-time warning in nft_pipapo_destroy() to catch unexpected non-empty gc_head state during teardown.
intent_record.what: A new statement, WARN_ON_ONCE(!list_empty(&priv->gc_head));, was added at the start of nft_pipapo_destroy() after local variable declarations and before dereferencing priv->match.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this emits a one-time kernel warning if priv->gc_head is not empty when the destroy path runs, helping detect unexpected pending garbage-collection entries during teardown without changing normal destruction flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a garbage-collection list head to `nft_pipapo` so it can queue deferred memory reclamation entries.
intent_record.what: A new documented field, `struct list_head gc_head;`, was added to `struct nft_pipapo`, and the struct comment was updated to describe it as a list of `nft_trans_gc` entries used to queue memory reclamation.
intent_record.how: This extends each `nft_pipapo` instance with storage for a garbage-collection queue head, enabling runtime tracking and deferred reclamation of `nft_trans_gc` objects associated with the set.

consistency_review.core_intent: Refactor nft_trans_gc batch-space handling by consolidating the simple remaining-capacity calculation into a reusable inline helper and removing the redundant wrapper function.
Ensure nft_set_pipapo garbage-collection state is correctly tracked and reliably queued after commit so deferred cleanup entries are flushed and processed.

relevance_review.reason: This change only refactors GC batch-space calculation helpers and removes a redundant wrapper. It does not affect when expired elements are freed relative to the live match-pointer swap, which is the core cause of the use-after-free.
This change only renames the GC helper and updates its comment. It does not alter when expired elements are freed or the commit-time/live-pointer swap behavior that caused the use-after-free.

These changes affect nft_set_pipapo commit-time GC behavior by ensuring expired-element cleanup is tracked and deferred/queued after commit, which is directly tied to the root cause of freeing elements too early before the live match pointer swap.

The root cause is premature freeing of expired elements before the live match pointer swap, causing UAF. This change only optimizes GC transaction batching/allocation behavior to avoid synchronizing on every expired element, and does not address when elements are freed relative to the live/clone swap.

The documented behavior is the corrected lifetime rule central to the bug: expired elements must be queued for reclamation only after the live `match` pointer is swapped, avoiding premature frees visible to readers of the old live structure.

The change directly modifies pipapo commit-time garbage collection behavior, using the scan-based GC routine during commit before publishing the cloned match structure. This is exactly the area implicated by the root cause: incorrect commit-time GC handling of expired elements in the clone leading to premature freeing and use-after-free against the old live match.

This change fixes initialization of the gc_head list head, preventing GC from operating on an uninitialized list. The root cause of the vulnerability is premature freeing of expired elements before the live match pointer swap, leading to UAF on still-visible old data. These are different issues.

This change only adds a teardown warning for unexpected non-empty gc_head state in nft_pipapo_destroy(). It does not change the commit-time GC behavior, element lifetime, or match-pointer swap ordering that caused the use-after-free.

Adding a GC list head to nft_pipapo enables deferred reclamation of expired elements instead of freeing them immediately during commit-time scanning, which directly addresses the premature free/use-after-free root cause.

candidates.rationale: This invokes garbage collection on the clone during commit before the live match pointer is swapped. Per the root cause, expiring and freeing elements at this point can free objects still reachable through the old live structure, leading to UAF for concurrent readers/dumpers.

This swap happens only after the prior GC call. The ordering embodied by this statement relative to the earlier GC is central to the bug: readers may still observe old until this replacement, so freeing expired elements before this point is unsafe.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs commit-time garbage collection on the clone before the live match pointer is replaced. As described in the root cause, this can free expired elements that are still reachable via the old live structure, causing a use-after-free for concurrent packet-path readers or dumpers.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full GC and commit interaction. The vulnerable construct is present in `pipapo_commit()` and `pipapo_gc()`. In `pipapo_commit()`, GC is run on the clone before the live `match` pointer is swapped: `if (time_after_eq(jiffies, priv->last_gc + nft_set_gc_interval(set))) pipapo_gc(set, priv->clone);` and only later `rcu_assign_pointer(priv->match, priv->clone);`. This exactly matches the root cause: expired elements are collected while `priv->match` still points to the old live structure that readers use. Inside `pipapo_gc()`, expired elements are actually removed and freed: after `pipapo_drop(m, rulemap);` it does `rcu_barrier(); nft_set_elem_destroy(set, e, true);`. Since `m` here is the clone passed from `pipapo_commit(set, priv->clone)`, freeing happens before the new clone becomes live, so readers on the old `match` or walkers/dumpers can still reach `e` from the old mapping tables. There is no fix present such as deferring destruction until after swapping `priv->match`, separating clone cleanup from element freeing, or walking the old live structure after an RCU-safe swap. Therefore the code contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
